_about: Authored words for the evaluation page of what M1 left over (endpoint card). Bundles are keyed by the judge's bundle name in gaps-endpoint.raw.json; if a bundle appears or vanishes, gen-gaps.js stops. Plain lines follow gabe-lens plain mode (../workflow-panel/plain-audit.py). Numbers are never typed here.

inventory.plain: A fact the lab already holds, so the work is a row in the inventory and a few lines in a panel.

lab.plain: A fact the map already produces, so the work is carrying it into the lab with its probe.

arm.plain: A fact no feed carries, so the work is new generation code with its test battery and a dry run on the four study apps.

outside.plain: A fact that reading code cannot produce, such as real traffic.

the-route-in-order.name: The route, in order
the-route-in-order.gain: The numbered steps of each ending, the checks it passed or fired, and the route that passes every check.

empty-means-what.name: What an empty slot means
empty-means-what.gain: An empty slot that tells a measured zero from a reading that never ran, plus the norm for each stage.

what-each-ending-carries.name: What each ending carries
what-each-ending-carries.gain: The rules behind the validation ending, and the headers each ending sends back.

whose-write.name: Whose write it is
whose-write.gain: The writes of the endpoint told apart from the writes of its login check, so the race alert stops firing almost everywhere.

honest-proof.name: Proof you can open
honest-proof.gain: Coverage words backed by what a test really asserted, in place of one word stamped by kind.

inside-the-calls.name: Inside the calls
inside-the-calls.gain: The functions behind a folded step, each with its raises, refusals, commits and roles.

how-common.name: How common each piece is
how-common.gain: The count of other endpoints that use the same piece, so the odd one out becomes visible.

field-rules-and-anchors.name: Field rules, and a line to open
field-rules-and-anchors.gain: The rule beside each field of a shape, and a file and line on every block.

why-a-touch-why-it-survives.name: Why a touch happens, and why it survives
why-a-touch-why-it-survives.gain: The condition on each table touch, and the commit or rollback that decided the fate of a write.

what-the-screen-does.name: What the screen does on each ending
what-the-screen-does.gain: The message, redirect or retry the user gets for each ending.

alive-during-the-request.name: What stays alive during the request
alive-during-the-request.gain: The values held only while a request runs, and the ones the server keeps between requests.

B-provisions.label: Provisions
B-provisions.question: Why does a refused request still show a committed write?
B-provisions.plain: A users row the login check adds before the handler runs, on almost every endpoint.

B-race.label: Race on a unique key
B-race.question: Which unique inserts of this endpoint's own code have no catch around them?
B-race.plain: An alert that fires almost everywhere today, because it counts the login check's insert too.

B-cases.label: Cases
B-cases.question: Which tests came to this endpoint on purpose, and which only passed through?
B-cases.plain: Two case lists that disagree today, neither saying what a test came here to do.

B-entity-cluster.label: Entity · cluster
B-entity-cluster.question: Is this endpoint filed under the entity its tables belong to?
B-entity-cluster.plain: The crumb you already navigate by, so a row of its own only repeats the frame.

B-signature.label: Signature
B-signature.question: Does this handler differ from the norm of the app, in being async or in its size?
B-signature.plain: Three fragments with better homes, and an async mark that separates nothing in this app.

B-rate-limit.label: Rate limit
B-rate-limit.question: Which rate tier does this endpoint sit on, against the rest of the app?
B-rate-limit.plain: A cap that never changes what the code decides, though its tier is a real choice per endpoint.

B-journeys.label: Journeys · workflow step
B-journeys.question: Which step comes before this endpoint in its named walk, and which comes after?
B-journeys.plain: One useful line of before and after, mixed with broad tests that only pass through.

B-steps-longest.label: Steps in the longest chain
B-steps-longest.plain: A maximum of numbers the chain already shows one per ending, so the row adds nothing once the chain has one.

B-usage-fan-in.label: Usage · fan-in
B-usage-fan-in.plain: A count that is the length of the list of screens that fetch the endpoint, so it belongs on that row.

do.plain: A piece of work to start now, in the order of the cards.

later.plain: A piece of work worth doing, after the ones marked do.

dropb.plain: A piece of work that is not worth its cost.

keep.plain: An attribute that stays on the card as a row of its own.

demote.plain: An attribute that stays in the data and shows only on hover or inside another row.

dropa.plain: An attribute that leaves the inventory.

imp.plain: The highest importance among the gaps this work closes, by your depth rule.

grid.plain: A piece of work, placed by what it costs and how much it decides.

grid: The upper left corner is where to start: work that costs hours and closes gaps rated 3.
{nHours} of the {nBundles} pieces cost hours, because the map already produces the fact and only the inventory never named it.
Nothing on this page grades the code. Each piece adds a fact about what is there and how it behaves.
attrs: {nKeep} attributes earn a question of their own and stay. {nDemote} stay in the data and leave the card's rows. {nDrop} leave the inventory.
The entity and the URL group stay as navigation, the way you already use them, and stop being a row.

wrong.title: One picture in the lab is wrong today
wrong.plain: The Security panel lists the three app-wide checks in the order the code registers them, and they run in the reverse order.
wrong.fix: The first piece of work corrects it, because the route already carries the true order.

labels.A-Q10: column facts of a table, which belong on the table's card
